# AGENTS.md — turnstile

## Branching & releases (standing instruction, Oct 2026)

- `dev` is the default and the only primary development branch; it is
  GitHub-protected (required `ci` status check, no direct pushes). All work
  lands in `dev` via PR — never push directly, never commit to `main`.
- `main` is release-only. It is promoted exclusively by a `dev` → `main`
  PR that a human merges deliberately. Do not merge anything into `main`,
  and do not click through a dev→main PR merge, unless the user asks
  explicitly in the session.
- Keep local `main` as a read-only mirror of `origin/main`; branch feature
  work from `dev`.

## What this repo is

OpenCode v2 promise-plugin: `turnstile.ts` is the thin entry point the host
loads; behavior lives in focused modules under `src/`, one boundary per
file — the authoritative module map (every file + responsibility) is
`docs/modules.md`; do not hand-copy it here.
It
mechanically enforces an agent pipeline (planner → plan-reviewer →
executor → test-runner → reviewer). The orchestrator policy is injected
into the parent session at runtime by the plugin (from `src/policy.ts`) —
primarily via the `session.context` channel, with the `execute.after` hook
as the fallback re-supply — rather than written to any instructions
file at install time; a fresh install can never lose it; per-agent
instruction lines live in each `agents/<name>.md`.
The plugin and pipeline subagent definitions are installed by
`npm run init` (symlinks by default, `--copy` for real copies; manifest:
`install.json`), making this repo the source of truth for
`~/.config/opencode/plugin(s)`, `~/.config/opencode/agents`, and
`~/.config/opencode/skills` (the vendored `turnstile-init`, `turnstile-on`,
`turnstile-off`, `turnstile-evidence`, `turnstile-config`,
`turnstile-status`, `turnstile-log`, `turnstile-prov`, and
`turnstile-prov-views` skills).
The subagent definitions the pipeline dispatches (planner, plan-reviewer,
executor, test-runner, reviewer, debugger) ship as examples in
`agents/`;
`npm run init` links or copies them into `~/.config/opencode/agents/`;
the shipped definitions carry no `model:` frontmatter — subagents inherit
the dispatching session's model, and per-agent pins belong in
`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` under `agents.<name>.model`; installs
never carry user state.
`--print-model-config` optionally prints a ready-to-paste `{"agents": {…}}`
model snippet (repeatable `--model [name=]provider/model[#variant]` seeds;
model ids may be multi-segment, e.g. `oMLX/oQ/GLM-5.3-Flash-oQ4-mtp`;
`--validate` checks concrete specs against `opencode models` and exits 1 on a
miss; `--model`/`--validate` given without `--print-model-config` exit 2) and
writes nothing — `install.mjs` prints the snippet and short-circuits before
any manifest work (see the README).
Verification tooling: ESLint + typescript-eslint (lint), Prettier
(format), `tsc` strict (typecheck), and `scripts/check-markers.mjs` (marker
drift). `npm test` enforces 100% line, branch, and function coverage over
`src/` + `turnstile.ts` via node:test's built-in V8 coverage thresholds
(100 for lines, branches, and functions) with `--experimental-test-isolation=none` — fully
deterministic on a green suite: a red branch report is a real
never-executed decision, never a merge artifact — the installer scripts
(`bin/`, `scripts/`) are outside the gate:

```
npm run ci           # ci:host (lint -> format:check -> typecheck -> check:markers -> test) — host chain only
npm run ci:installed # install:check — install-drift, run after npm run init
```

## Coding practices

These rules are enforced on every change, not aspirational. A review that
spots a violation rejects the change or refactors it in the same change set —
"cleanup later" is not an option.

### Writing style — ISO 24495-1 (standing instruction, Nov 2026)

All prose written in this repo must follow ISO 24495-1 (Plain language —
Part 1: Governing principles and guidelines). This applies everywhere prose
is written: documentation (README, `docs/`), docstrings/JSDoc, code comments,
commit messages, and agent/skill definition text. Prioritize the standard's
core principles: write for your readers, keep it findable and usable, and
say only what's needed — nothing more.

### Functional design (function size cap)

Functions should be small, focused, and easy to understand. Hard guideline:
**a function is at most 20–30 lines** (clean-code best practice; the tighter
20 is the target, 30 is the ceiling before a refactor is mandatory). If a
function exceeds it, break it down by the concerns inside it — extraction is
not optional past the ceiling. A function that needs a comment to explain its
structure is already too big. (In this repo, behavior already splits one
concern per file under `src/`; keep new logic in the boundary that owns it,
not in `turnstile.ts`, which stays a thin entry point.)

### DRY (don't repeat yourself)

No duplicated logic. The same decision, rule, constant, or transformation
lives in exactly one place; a second occurrence of non-trivial logic is a
defect, not a shortcut. Concretely in this repo:

- A value already derived in one boundary is passed in, not recomputed in
  another (e.g. a computed path or count is threaded as a parameter, not
  rebuilt at each call site).
- Marker syntax, config defaults, and policy text each have one canonical
  source (`src/markers.ts`, `src/config.ts`, `src/policy.ts`); anything that
  needs them imports or is checked against the source by
  `scripts/check-markers.mjs` — never copy them by hand.
- When a repeated block appears a third time, extract it in the same change
  set that added it. A comment like "keep these in sync" marks a DRY
  violation to fix, not a convention to follow.

### Architectural alignment (SOLID)

Follow SOLID principles. Each module or component should have a single,
well-defined responsibility. Avoid tight coupling between modules. (The
`src/` boundaries are the architecture: `gates.ts` decides, `markers.ts`
parses, `state.ts` remembers, `ledger.ts` persists and evicts, `journal.ts`
persists, the `hooks-*` modules carry the per-surface hook bodies, and
`setup.ts` wires.
Dependencies flow one way; no cycles. New behavior extends existing
boundaries through their exported interfaces — a boundary is never reached
into or bypassed to avoid touching its API.)

### Security

- Never store secrets in code
- Validate all user input
- Use parameterized queries for database operations
- Keep dependencies updated

### Performance awareness

Write efficient code by default. Profile before optimizing. Avoid premature
optimization but be mindful of algorithmic complexity.

### Testing

Write tests for critical paths and complex logic. Aim for high test coverage
on business logic. Use descriptive test names that explain the expected
behavior. All tests should have docstrings too. (The gate state machine in `src/state.ts` and `src/markers.ts` is
the critical path; the harness is `node:test` with
`--experimental-strip-types --experimental-test-isolation=none`, wired into `npm run ci`.
Coverage is enforced at 100% lines, branches, and functions over `src/` +
`turnstile.ts` by the same command — a coverage extension is not needed, the
Node test runner's built-in thresholds gate it, and with `--experimental-test-isolation=none`
a green suite is deterministic: a red branch report is a real
never-executed decision, never a merge artifact. `bin/` and `scripts/` sit
outside the gate.)

### Error handling

Handle errors explicitly and provide meaningful error messages. Log errors
appropriately without exposing sensitive information to users. (This repo's
contract: fail open; journal internal errors, never throw from hooks except
the deliberate `BLOCKED by turnstile:` enforcement messages.)

### Intentional commenting

Write comments only when necessary. Code should be self-explanatory through
clear naming and structure. Comments should explain "why" not "what".
(All functions carry Google-standard JSDoc with fully typed parameters and
returns; the doc comment atop `turnstile.ts` is a contract-level summary
pointing at `docs/architecture.md` (the entry-point index into the
section files under `docs/architecture/`), the authoritative detailed
reference.)

Comments and docstrings must be self-contained: a reader without the plan,
the issue, or this session's context must still understand them. Never
reference chunks, acceptance criteria, plan files, or issue numbers in
source comments, docstrings, or test titles — those citations belong in the
plan file and the commit message, not the code.

### Naming conventions

Use descriptive, self-documenting names for variables, functions, and
classes. Follow language-specific conventions (camelCase for TypeScript).

### Formatting

Follow language-specific formatting standards. Use consistent indentation
and spacing. (Enforced mechanically by Prettier, `npm run format`, except
the marker regex literals in `src/markers.ts`, which are `prettier-ignore`d
because `scripts/check-markers.mjs` extracts them as single lines.)

### Dependencies

Minimize the use of external dependencies. Only add dependencies that are
absolutely necessary for the project. (Zero runtime dependencies is a
stated feature; devDependencies are tooling only.)

## Plugin contract (do not break silently)

- Module shape: default export `{ id: "turnstile", server, setup }`. `id`
  must stay `"turnstile"`. `server` is a legacy v1 shim kept only for loaders
  that require it; the factory is exported as `turnstile`.
- `src/` and `tests/` must stay erasable TypeScript (no enums, namespaces,
  parameter properties); the test harness runs the real source through
  `node --experimental-strip-types`.
- Host API is the v2 shape
  `{ tool.hook, session.hook, permission.hook, event.subscribe }`, verified
  against opencode v2.0.22. If hooks don't fire, check the host version before
  assuming a logic bug.
- `docs/architecture.md` is the entry point to the authoritative reference
  for enforced contracts (the section files live under `docs/architecture/`);
  the doc comment atop `turnstile.ts` is a contract-level summary that points
  at it, and its module list must track `src/`.

## Enforcement behavior (easy to regress)

- Fail-open by design: every hook body is guarded; internal errors are
  journaled, never block tool calls. Only deliberate `BLOCKED by turnstile:`
  errors throw. Keep that distinction when editing hooks.
- Journal replay: `GATE: PASS` entries from `~/.local/share/opencode/metrics/turnstile.jsonl`
  and the per-session `sessions/<parentID>.jsonl` sinks restore gate state on
  restart (the newest `replayTailLines` lines, default
  2000, walked across journal generations newest-first and merged
  ts-ordered across sinks), and plan-reviewer
  `VERDICT: APPROVE` entries restore the plan-approval gate the same way.
  A new user prompt resets the session's gate state, unless
  `continuationCarry` re-arms the one-prompt grace for a same-worktree/branch
  continuation carrying earned credit (a journaled `GATE: PASS` or a credited
  reviewer `VERDICT: APPROVE`; a retired plan-bound task whose review was
  interrupted mid-flight — green gate, ≥1 counted reviewer dispatch or a
  waived reviewer round, no credited approval — carries the same way,
  journaled as a `recovery: true` continuation row); replay-time
  `refusedApprove:true` last-wins
  suppression still outranks the carried approval.
- Marker regexes (`GATE: PASS|FAIL tests=…`, `VERDICT: APPROVE|BLOCK …`) are
  parsed from task results and child-session text. Changing marker syntax
  requires updating both the regexes here and the marker examples in the
  validated sources — README.md, `docs/usage.md` (the usage index, which
  carries the canonical marker-example block), `agents/*.md`, and
  `src/policy.ts` — checked together by `scripts/check-markers.mjs`.
- The read-counter keys off the parent session (`childToParent` map); state
  is per parent, not per child subagent session.
- Shipped agent definitions (`agents/*.md`) must treat configured values as
  defaults, not constants: where a definition names a path that maps to a
  config key (`.opencode/plans/` → `plansDir`), the surrounding instruction
  must say to honor a path given in the dispatch prompt and name the
  config key so a customized setup doesn't strand the agent. Frontmatter
  permission rules that mirror a default (planner's `.opencode/plans/**`
  allow) carry a comment stating they must be updated when the key changes.
  `.opencode/knowledge/` is exempt — it is a repo-local convention, not a
  turnstile config key. When a config default changes, check `agents/*.md`
  phrasing in the same change set.

## Operational notes

- Journals live outside the repo at `~/.local/share/opencode/metrics/`
  (`turnstile.jsonl` and each `sessions/<parentID>.jsonl` rotate at 5 MB,
  5 generations per file). Retention is bounded:
  2 files × (1 current + 5 generations) × 5 MB ≈ ~30 MB per journal, worst
  case ~60 MB total, plus one bounded sink per live parent session. With
  `trace: false` the trace file is never written,
  roughly halving that; the JSONL journal is the audit trail and always
  writes.
- Executor dispatch blocking scans `.opencode/plans/*.md` in the project dir
  for `## Decomposition`; plans there are load-bearing, not scratch files.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` is the contributor-facing summary of the rules in this
  file (dev loop, marker-drift source set, erasable TS, fail-open,
  dependencies, architecture-docs sync). When a rule here changes, update
  CONTRIBUTING.md in the same change set; if a rule lives only here, leave
  CONTRIBUTING.md pointing at this file rather than duplicating it.
- `npm test` is the sole coverage authority. `scripts/branch-coverage.mjs` is
  diagnostic-only — it localizes what `npm test` already flagged (file:line +
  snippet); never loop on its output, never treat its findings as a work
  queue, and do not write ad-hoc V8-parsing scripts to re-derive coverage
  the gate already enforces; if per-file attribution is needed, run a single
  test file with the same `node --test` invocation the gate uses.
  `test:stable`-style retry aliases are forbidden by design: the gate is
  deterministic, so a red run is a real gap.

## Architecture docs (keep in sync when code changes)

`docs/architecture.md` (the entry-point index, with the section files under
`docs/architecture/` and `docs/images/*.svg` rendered from
`docs/diagrams/*.d2`) is the living architecture reference for new users and
devs. It is not a snapshot: when a change alters what the diagrams or
document describe, update them in the same change set — not as a follow-up.

- **Trigger for updates** — touch the docs when a change affects any of:
  - the module map (`docs/modules.md`): new/renamed/removed files under
    `src/`, or changed dependency direction between boundaries;
  - the hook surface: hooks registered in `src/setup.ts` (session, tool,
    permission, event types handled), or what fires on each hook;
  - enforcement: gates added/removed/renamed, `GateState` fields, block
    reasons, caps/budgets/defaults, marker semantics;
  - persistence (`docs/journal.md` entry point and its section files under
    `docs/journal/`): journal entry types, replay behavior,
    rotation, the `opencode-turnstile status` output;
  - configuration: keys, defaults, validation, or the layered resolution.
    Refactors that move code without changing behavior (renames aside) don't
    require doc edits.
- **How to update** — edit the D2 source in `docs/diagrams/` (not the SVG),
  re-render the matching image, and update the matching architecture doc
  (the index or a section file under `docs/architecture/`) to match:

  ```sh
  d2 --theme 200 docs/diagrams/d01-modules.d2 docs/images/d01-modules.svg
  ```

  Commit the source, the rendered SVG, and the doc together. Keep the
  diagram identities stable: `d01-modules` (module map), `d02-hooks` (hook
  surface), `d03-task-flow` (end-to-end sequence), `d04-gate-state` (state
  machine), `d05-persistence` (journal/replay). Add a new numbered diagram
  rather than overloading an existing one. The README hero banner
  (`docs/images/hero.svg`) is the exception: it is hand-authored SVG with no
  D2 source — edit the SVG directly (keep it valid XML, dark theme, wide
  aspect), and update it whenever enforcement points change.

- **Same accuracy bar as code** — diagrams cite real function/hook/field
  names; if a name in a diagram no longer exists in source, that's a bug in
  the docs. The doc's claims are verified against source the same way test
  expectations are.
- **CONTRIBUTING.md stays aligned too** — it mirrors the repo rules in
  short form (dev loop, marker-drift source set, architecture-docs rule).
  When a change above makes CONTRIBUTING.md's claims stale — the CI chain
  composition, the set of marker-validated sources, or the docs-sync rule —
  update it in the same change set. CONTRIBUTING.md defers detail to this
  file; keep it a summary, not a second source of truth.
- **`examples/turnstile.example.json` mirrors `defaultConfig()`** — the
  example carries every key from the defaults in `src/config.ts` verbatim,
  with exactly one deliberate omission (`metricsDir`, computed at load
  time). When a default value, key, or sub-block (`agents`, `toolPolicy`,
  `gitGates`) changes in `defaultConfig()`, update the example in the same
  change set, including the marker regex sources when `GATE_RE` /
  `VERDICT_RE` change. The README documents the example as matching the
  code defaults, so a stale example is a documented-behavior bug, not just
  a stale snippet.

# Turnstile config

Display the user's turnstile configuration read-only. Never apply edits —
point at `examples/turnstile.example.json` (every key except the computed
`metricsDir`) and the config table in `docs/usage/configuration.md` instead.

## Steps

1. Locate the raw config file: the `TURNSTILE_CONFIG` env var if set, else
   `~/.config/opencode/turnstile.json`. If the file is absent, report "no
   config file (all defaults in effect)".

2. Show the file's contents — the full JSON, verbatim, in a fenced code
   block (or the plain text for non-JSON formats). The report must always
   include the raw file contents, not only a summary of overrides. If the
   file is absent, show nothing and say all defaults are in effect.

3. Cross-check the resolved values against `status --json` (detect context:
   inside the turnstile repo use `node bin/cli.mjs status --json`; elsewhere
   `npx opencode-turnstile status --json`) — its `suspension.configPath` and
   `suspension.configFilePresent` confirm which file the CLI consulted.

4. Compare the raw overrides against the defaults table (docs/usage/configuration.md)
   and mark each key as overridden or default.

5. Report `metricsDir` as computed at load time — it is deliberately absent
   from `examples/turnstile.example.json`.

6. Surface any `[turnstile] config:` warnings from the journal — the actual
   wording is `config: unknown key "…" ignored` or
   `config: invalid value for "…"; keeping default`.

7. If the user names any status options, forward them to the CLI invocation.
   If the CLI rejects an option, surface the usage error verbatim; never
   retry blind, never drop the flag.

# Turnstile evidence

Evidence bundles correlate a task's journaled gate state into a shareable
artifact: the green gate, the plan approval, the reviewer ensemble, and the
journal integrity anchor. A bundle is **a correlated claim, not proof — say
so wherever it is posted**.

## When to use

- Publishing earned state for a task (PR description, sticky comment).
- Inspecting what the journal recorded for a task handle.
- A pre-landing self-check that the ensemble bar was actually met.

## Reading a bundle

- Task handle: `t-<8 hex>` (the journal's task identity).
- `green: true` marks the earned green-gate flag.
- The plan/tests/review sections carry the journaled counts: the reviewer
  ensemble must show 2 unwaived reviewer approvals under the default
  `reviewEnsemble: enforce`, plus the waiver/block/dispatch counts.
- `journal.head` is the sha integrity anchor for the journal tail the bundle
  was built from.

## Publishing

Detect context: inside the turnstile repo use `node bin/cli.mjs evidence`;
elsewhere `npx opencode-turnstile evidence`.

- `--format markdown` renders the shareable bundle.
- `--out <name>` writes the `.json` bundle plus a sibling `.md`.
- `--validate` re-checks an existing bundle without writing anything.

If the user names any other options, forward them to the CLI invocation
verbatim. If the CLI rejects an option, surface the usage error verbatim;
never retry blind, never drop the flag.

# Turnstile init

Install the turnstile plugin and the pipeline agent definitions into the
user's `~/.config/opencode` and verify the install. The orchestrator policy
is injected at runtime by the plugin (`src/policy.ts`) — nothing is written
to any instructions file, ever.

Two contexts this skill can run in; detect which one you are in first:

- **Inside the turnstile git repo** (a `.git` directory plus a `package.json`
  with an `init` script): use the repo commands `npm run init` /
  `npm run install:check`. Symlink mode is the default there — the checkout
  stays the source of truth.
- **Anywhere else** (npm-package or npx context): use the CLI,
  `npx opencode-turnstile init` / `npx opencode-turnstile check`. Do NOT run
  `npm run init` — that script only exists in the repo. The install mode is
  resolved from an explicit flag, then the manifest's `mode` field, then
  auto-detect: a `.git` checkout installs by linking, a package install
  copies.

## Steps

1. Install:

   - In the repo: `npm run init`
   - Elsewhere: `npx opencode-turnstile init`

   Don't override the mode unless a step fails. Use `--copy` only when the
   user refuses symlinks or the install target is a dotfiles repo that
   rejects them (repo: `npm run init -- --copy`; CLI:
   `npx opencode-turnstile init --copy`). Copy mode records everything in a
   ledger (`~/.config/opencode/.turnstile-install.json`).

   Targets come from `install.json`; unowned files in the target directories
   are never touched. Conflicts (a real file differing from the repo, or a
   user-edited copy) fail with a per-path summary. Show the user the output
   and stop — don't force anything with `--force` without asking.

2. Verify — must exit 0:

   - In the repo: `npm run install:check` (add `-- --copy` for copy mode)
   - Elsewhere: `npx opencode-turnstile check`

   Drift or a conflict is reported per path; `check --repair` prints a
   write-free "would repair" dry run, and `install --repair` auto-fixes

   prompt that would be refused.

3. Otherwise compose a copy-ready prompt for the user, e.g.:

   > Send this yourself (do not let the agent send it):
   > `<suspendMarker> <the user's stated reason>`

   State plainly that the marker is honored only from the user's own typed
   prompt — relaying it as the agent does nothing.

4. If the user names any status options, forward them to the CLI invocation.
   If the CLI rejects an option, surface the usage error verbatim; never
   retry blind, never drop the flag.

## Mechanics (one sentence)

While suspended, deliberate gate blocks stop being enforced but every
would-block is journaled, no gate credit is earned, and the suspension
survives a restart.

Report the decisions made, from the turnstile decision ledger. Read-only —
never modify config or journals from this skill.

## Steps

1. Detect context: inside the turnstile repo use `node bin/cli.mjs prov`;
   elsewhere `npx opencode-turnstile prov`. It walks the shared journal and
   the session sinks and prints `prov:*` rows oldest-first; it handles
   missing/rotated files and exits 0 with no output on an empty ledger. The
   CLI has two modes: rendering (`prov [sessionID] [--json] [--tail <n>]`)
   and verification (`prov --verify`, or `prov --verify --session <id>` for
   a scoped check with per-row inclusion proofs).
2. Scope: with no sessionID the ledger covers every session. When the user
   asks about a specific session or time range, pass the sessionID, and
   default to `--tail 200` so the report stays readable; otherwise default
   to `--tail 50`. If the user names other options (e.g. `--tail 100`,
   `--json`), forward them verbatim to the invocation; if the CLI rejects
   one, surface the usage error verbatim — never retry blind, never drop
   the flag.
3. Verify on request: when the user asks whether the ledger — or one
   session's decision record — is intact, tamper-evident, or anchored,
   invoke the verify mode instead of the reporting mode (scoped
   `--session <id>` when they name a session, adding `--json` if asked).
   Report the verdict (chain ok / first broken link / unanchored refs) and,
   in scoped mode, the per-row facts (row hash, epoch, `merkleOk`, anchored
   status, weakest trust domain). Surface exit codes: 0 intact, 1 broken or
   unanchored, 2 usage error. Read-only — verify writes nothing.
4. Report the decisions, grouped per session and in order:
   - `prov:stated` — a human prompt: quote the redacted text, but skip rows
     that are pure pipeline chatter ("continue", bare acknowledgements)
     unless the user asked for the unfiltered record — the raw row is the
     source of truth, so note how many were skipped.
   - `prov:denied` — a human permission denial: report the ask kind
     (plan / landing / hands-on) as a decision the human made.
   - `prov:waiver` — a human gate waiver: report the covered stages.
5. Summarize what the record shows about judgment in the loop: what the
   human directed, what they refused, and any gap (e.g. a session missing
   from the ledger) — but do not editorialize beyond what the rows say.
   Prompt text is already secret-redacted at capture; never attempt to
   un-redact or infer redacted content.

# turnstile

[![ci](https://github.com/edseabolt/turnstile/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/edseabolt/turnstile/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/opencode-turnstile)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencode-turnstile)
[![coverage](https://img.shields.io/badge/coverage-100%25%20lines%20%C2%B7%20branches%20%C2%B7%20funcs-brightgreen)](package.json)
[![deps](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime%20dependencies-0-brightgreen)](package.json)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/opencode-turnstile)](LICENSE)

![turnstile runs the ensemble end to end: planner → plan-reviewer → executor → test-runner → reviewer, with blocked dispatches (red) until VERDICT: APPROVE and verified GATE: PASS evidence flip each gate green, and every decision lands in turnstile.jsonl](docs/images/demo.svg)

**Verify what your agents claim.** An agent that says "tests pass" is asking
you to trust it. Turnstile checks instead: dispatches that would violate the
pipeline throw `BLOCKED by turnstile: <reason>` until a real `GATE: PASS` and
a plan-reviewer `VERDICT: APPROVE` exist, and every decision appends to an
auditable JSONL journal (`npx opencode-turnstile status` shows the trail).
Decisions happen in tool and task-dispatch hooks, outside the model loop.
Zero runtime dependencies, fails open.

Turnstile is an [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) v2 promise-plugin that
mechanically enforces an agent pipeline: planner → plan-reviewer → executor →
test-runner → reviewer, with a gate at every hand-off. The orchestrator policy
is injected at runtime by the plugin; nothing is written to any instructions
file.

- Quick start: [below](#tldr--try-it-in-two-minutes)
- The walkthrough: [using it for real work](#using-it-for-real-work)
- How it works inside: [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md)
- Day-to-day reference (waivers, config, journals, install modes):
  [`docs/usage.md`](docs/usage.md)

## TL;DR — try it in two minutes

```sh
npx opencode-turnstile init      # install the plugin + pipeline agents
npx opencode-turnstile check     # verify the install (incl. plugin loadability); must exit 0
```

Then **restart OpenCode** (or `opencode service restart`) so the plugin
loads. Adding just the plugin still enforces the gates, but the pipeline
needs agents to dispatch against, so run `init` (or bring your own, see
[`docs/usage/install.md`](docs/usage/install.md#customizing-the-pipeline-agents)):

```jsonc
// ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json
{ "plugins": ["opencode-turnstile"] }
```

After restart the orchestrator dispatches the pipeline on your prompts,
blocked work says `BLOCKED by turnstile: <reason>` instead of proceeding,
and every decision is journaled — see it with
`npx opencode-turnstile status`. To bypass the gates for a task, put
`USER WAIVER:` in **your own prompt**.

## Using it for real work

You never invoke the pipeline stages directly. Start a task the way you
already would, and the enforcement wraps it. The one habit to build: open
with the planner.

![turnstile — the enforced pipeline: planner → plan-reviewer → executor → test-runner → reviewer, with gates blocking every dispatch](docs/images/hero.svg)

**1. Start a task by invoking the planner.** Paste an issue or a topic into
your prompt and ask for a plan:

```text
Work on issue #42 (flaky retry in the upload path). Start from the planner:
produce a plan with a decomposition, then run the pipeline through review.
```

The planner writes a plan with numbered `AC-n` / `chunk-N` entries to
`.opencode/plans/`. From here the pipeline drives itself — the `PIPELINE:`
status line on each result names the next stage:

```text
PIPELINE: planner=done plan=PENDING tests=RED reviewer=0/2
next=plan-reviewer — dispatch the next agent in this same turn
```

**2. The plan gate fires.** The plan-reviewer must record `VERDICT: APPROVE`
before any executor dispatch is allowed. A `VERDICT: BLOCK` sends the work
back to the planner — nothing for you to do unless you want to override:

```text
PLAN APPROVED: ship it as-is, the retry heuristic is good enough for now
```

(in your prompt — see [Waivers and approvals](#waivers-and-approvals)).

**3. The executor is gated on the approved plan** and must cite `chunk-N` /
`AC-n` entries from the decomposition, so implementation traces to the plan.

**4. Tests gate the reviewer.** The test-runner must emit
`GATE: PASS tests=…` and a matching exit-0 test execution must exist in the
task's history.

**5. The reviewer closes the loop.** Approval requires two unwaived reviewer
dispatches (ensemble); once credited, the landing gate releases `git push`.
A provably no-op push is exempt by default (`emptyDiffExempt`).

Enforcement is dormant until engaged: turnstile arms when your prompt
provides a plan or asks to run the planner/pipeline, and sleeps again on task
completion or `TURNSTILE OFF:` (`alwaysEnforce: true` restores always-armed).
Once engaged there is no audit-only mode. Per-feature opt-outs are listed in
[Configuration](#configuration).

When a gate fires early, the block message names the reason:

```text
BLOCKED by turnstile: no plan approval for "<plan path>". Dispatch the
plan-reviewer subagent first; proceed with executor only after the
plan-reviewer's first line is `VERDICT: APPROVE crit=<n> high=<n> med=<n>
low=<n>`, or obtain an explicit user waiver (a user prompt this task must
contain the literal marker 'USER WAIVER:' followed by the user's words).
```

A full annotated session, with every dispatch, block message, waiver, and
the journal entries behind them, is in
[`docs/usage/worked-session.md`](docs/usage/worked-session.md).

## What it enforces

Gates are decided in `execute.before` hooks; every gate has a human escape
hatch. Full detail (guards, state fields, escape ladders, diagrams) lives in
[`docs/architecture/gates.md`](docs/architecture/gates.md).

| Gate                   | In one line                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Plan approval          | `executor` dispatches blocked while the plans dir holds a pending plan (no reviewer `VERDICT: APPROVE` or human approval); editing the plan's spec region invalidates an earlier approval |
| Reviewer dispatch gate | `reviewer` dispatches blocked until a `GATE: PASS` verified by a real exit-0 test execution in this task                                                                                  |
| Reviewer round cap     | Max 2 `reviewer` dispatches per task; waived dispatches bypass and don't count                                                                                                            |
| Reviewer ensemble      | A reviewer APPROVE credits the landing gate only at ≥2 unwaived reviewer dispatches                                                                                                       |
| Loop caps              | Per task: planner 3, plan-reviewer 3, test-runner 4, 16 total dispatches; exhaustion blocks and journals an `escalation` entry                                                            |
| Decomposition gate     | `executor` dispatches must cite `chunk-N` / `AC-n` when a plan has a `## Decomposition` block                                                                                             |
| Read horizon           | Warns at 8 whole-file `read` calls per session, blocks at 15 (prefer grep/glob)                                                                                                           |
| Tool-call policy       | `bash`/`shell` commands and `write`/`edit` paths matched against a configured denylist (default empty — the empty lists are the off switch)                                               |
| Commit-lint            | `git commit -m` subjects must be conventional commits when `gitGates.commitMessages` is on (default)                                                                                      |
| Landing gate           | `git push` without a credited reviewer `VERDICT: APPROVE` blocks; a repeat attempt forces the interactive human ask                                                                       |
| Marker parsing         | `GATE:` / `VERDICT:` markers parsed from task results and child text; only marker-contracted emitters flip state — echoes are journaled `suppressed`                                      |
| Trace & telemetry      | JSONL journal of dispatches, gate transitions, verdicts, blocked calls, errors                                                                                                            |
| Decoding clamps        | reviewer/plan-reviewer temperature = 0; executor/test-runner/debugger ≤ 0.2                                                                                                               |
| Compaction             | Injects a "preserve verbatim" instruction, then the live gate-state snapshot — de-tokenized so it can never re-parse as a marker                                                          |

A few behaviors worth knowing; the mechanics live in
[`docs/architecture/gates.md`](docs/architecture/gates.md) and
[`docs/architecture/hooks.md`](docs/architecture/hooks.md):

- **State lifecycle.** A new user prompt resets the session's gate state,
  except when continuation carry (default on) re-arms it for a prompt in the
  same worktree/branch with earned credit. An interrupted review carries the
  same way: the task re-opens with its green gate, dispatch counts, and plan
  approval intact.
- **Maintenance dispatches.** A bookkeeping-only executor dispatch (plan file
  named in the prompt, diff touching only docs/prose surfaces) skips the
  plan-approval and decomposition gates — capped at 4 per plan; any
  `src/`, `tests/`, `bin/`, `scripts/`, or config touch gates it as ordinary
  implementation work.
- **Parent hands-on edits.** Direct `write`/`edit` calls in the parent (and
  any non-pipeline subagent) are always gated: the first block throws, a
  repeat attempt raises a human permission ask (`always` / `once` /
  `reject`). Writes to the platform temp directory are exempt scratch.
- **Parent file-writing bash.** Confident file-writing bash commands
  (redirects from writer commands, `tee f`, `sed -i`, `cp`/`mv`/`dd`/…) run
  the same ladder; output capture never gates. `toolPolicy.bashWriteGate:
false` opts out (telemetry continues).

## Waivers and approvals

Turnstile reads a waiver or a human plan approval only from the user's own
prompt — the plugin checks which channel the marker arrived through, never
what an agent's dispatch prompt says.

- **`USER WAIVER:`** in your prompt waives gates; naming agent stages scopes
  it. The landing gate is not waiver-released: `git push` always needs the
  credited reviewer verdict or your permission reply.
- **`PLAN APPROVED:`** in your prompt approves the plan like a reviewer
  verdict, with human provenance; it replays across restart.
- **Permission escalation.** A retried landing or hands-on attempt escalates
  to you through OpenCode's permission surface — reply `always`, `once`, or
  `reject`. Turnstile assumes a human answers these asks; an auto-accepting
  host (`session.permissions: "autoaccept"`) degrades them to delays, one
  reason `"block"` is the default.

Full lifecycle semantics: [`docs/usage/waivers.md`](docs/usage/waivers.md).

## User plan review (opt-in)

With `planUserReview: true`, turnstile inserts a human checkpoint after the
planner: the plan-reviewer dispatch blocks until you answer from your own
prompt with **`PLAN REVIEWED:`** (accept; edit the plan file first if you
wish) or **`PLAN REJECTED:`** (retire the task scope). The literals work only
in your own prompt, waivers do not bypass the pause, and the pending state
survives a restart. Config: `planReviewAcceptMarker` /
`planReviewRejectMarker` rename the literals.

## Requirements phase (opt-in)

With `requirementsPhase: true`, an ungated requirements leg precedes the
planner for non-trivial tasks: a `requirements` subagent returns a spec with
numbered acceptance criteria and Open Questions; open questions come to you
before planning. The phase is soft — its only enforcement surface is a loop
cap (`maxRequirementsRounds`, default 2). Config: `agents.requirements`
renames the agent.

## Suspend and resume

Two prompt markers pause enforcement for the whole session, read only from
your own prompt:

- **`TURNSTILE OFF:`** suspends blocking: would-be blocks are journaled as
  `suspended` audit entries, but nothing throws and no ask is forced.
  The suspension survives a restart.
- **`TURNSTILE ON:`** resumes enforcement with fresh task state.

When both markers appear in one prompt, the later one wins. Config:
`suspendMarker` / `resumeMarker` rename the literals, and
`allowSuspend: false` disables both. Inspect the live state with
`node bin/cli.mjs status` (in-repo) or `npx opencode-turnstile status`.

### `opencode-turnstile log`

Prints a chronological, human-readable timeline of one session's journal,
ending with a summary line. Read-only.

    opencode-turnstile log                 # most recent session
    opencode-turnstile log <sessionID>     # a specific session
    opencode-turnstile log --json          # machine-readable output

### `opencode-turnstile prov`

Prints the decision-provenance ledger: `prov:stated` (every admitted parent
prompt, verbatim after mechanical secret redaction), `prov:denied` (human
permission denials), `prov:waiver` (human gate waivers), and `prov:override`
(a parent write/edit following a pipeline-child write to the same path).
Read-only; capture is dumb, derivation is offline.

    opencode-turnstile prov                 # every session, interleaved
    opencode-turnstile prov <sessionID>     # a specific session

Offline derived views over the decision ledger: classifies `prov:stated`
prompts by origin, computes the chatter noise rate, and aggregates

    opencode-turnstile prov-views <sessionID>     # a specific session
    opencode-turnstile prov-views --json          # machine-readable output

## Markers

Subagents must emit these as the first line of their output. These examples
are the canonical syntax; CI asserts the parser in `src/markers.ts` accepts
exactly them.

```
GATE: PASS tests=12 passed=12 failed=0
GATE: FAIL tests=12 passed=10 failed=2

VERDICT: APPROVE crit=0 high=0 med=2 low=1
VERDICT: BLOCK crit=1 high=0 med=0 low=2
```

The parser accepts these markers wrapped in markdown backticks and credits
them identically to the bare form; only a marker that does not match the
fields above is treated as absent.

Waiver and approval markers (must appear in the user's prompt, verbatim — a
dispatch prompt that merely contains the marker unlocks nothing):

```
USER WAIVER: <the user's words>
USER WAIVER: I approve proceeding to the <agent> stage
PLAN APPROVED: <the user's words>
```

## Install

Turnstile ships as the npm package
[`opencode-turnstile`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencode-turnstile).
Pick one way to install it; do not combine the plugin-array path with the
CLI install:

1. **Plugin only** — add `"plugins": ["opencode-turnstile"]` to
   `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` and restart. Gates enforce; agent
   definitions are not installed.
2. **Full install** — `npx opencode-turnstile init` installs the plugin and
   the pipeline agent definitions into `~/.config/opencode`.
3. **From a clone** — clone the repo and run `npm run init` (symlink mode)
   so installed artifacts stay live against your edits.

Turnstile has no npm lifecycle hooks: installing the package never writes to
`~/.config/opencode` — that happens only when you run an explicit command.
Modes, conflicts, the ledger, upgrades, uninstall, and per-agent model pins
are covered in [`docs/usage/install.md`](docs/usage/install.md).

Verify a clone with:

```sh
npm install
npm run ci            # lint, format:check, typecheck, check:markers, test gate enforcing 100% line/branch/function coverage
npm run ci:installed  # install:check — run after `npm run init` on a machine with artifacts
```

For behavior-preserving changes, `npm run test:differential` compares HEAD
against a reference commit scenario by scenario; the worked example lives in

The journal is per-machine; your teammates never see it. Turn the last

Commit the JSON and Markdown and a GitHub Action upserts one sticky comment

## What turnstile is not

Turnstile is a speed bump and an audit trail, not a security boundary. A
`GATE: PASS` is a claim correlated with evidence; the journal records what
was _claimed_ and is treated as sensitive data (see
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)); the denylist is a deterrent, not a sandbox; MCP

## Behavior contract

- Fail-open by design. Every hook body is guarded; internal errors are
  journaled and the tool call proceeds. The only thrown errors are the
  deliberate `BLOCKED by turnstile:` ones.
- `docs/architecture.md` (with the section files under `docs/architecture/`)
  is the authoritative reference for enforced contracts; the doc comment atop
  `turnstile.ts` summarizes it. CI keeps the marker examples in this README
  in sync with the parser regexes.
- Host API is the OpenCode v2 promise-plugin shape
  (`{ tool.hook, session.hook, permission.hook, event.subscribe }` — the
  permission hook is registered when the host exposes it).
- Host compatibility is checked at setup against the shipped range
  (`HOST_COMPAT` in `src/host-compat.ts`); see the matrix below.

### OpenCode compatibility matrix

| OpenCode host       | turnstile (current) | Status                                                                 |
| ------------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ≥ 2.0.22, < 3.0.0   | 0.15.x              | Supported (tested: 2.0.22, 2.0.27, 2.0.29, 2.2.0, 2.2.5, 2.2.7, 2.3.0) |
| ≥ 3.0.0 or < 2.0.22 | all                 | Refuses to enforce at setup; upgrade turnstile                         |
| version unreadable  | all                 | Enforces; one-time journal warning                                     |

On an incompatible host turnstile toasts the upgrade instruction and
registers no hooks (a full no-op — fail-open):

> turnstile 0.15.0 expects opencode >=2.0.22,<3.0.0; you're on 3.1.0 —
> upgrade turnstile (npm i opencode-turnstile@latest) or pin opencode

`npx opencode-turnstile status --check-updates` (opt-in, network, cached 24 h)
reports when a newer turnstile is published.

# Security Policy

## What turnstile is and is not

Turnstile is a speed bump and audit trail, not a security boundary. It
enforces process discipline over cooperative agents; it cannot constrain a
determined or hostile agent:

- Gate markers (`GATE: PASS tests=…`, `VERDICT: …`) are parsed from plain
  text. A marker emitted by a genuine contracted agent is trusted as to
  veracity — a hallucinated `GATE: PASS` from the real test-runner flips gate
  state (under the default `gateEvidence:enforce` a PASS additionally needs a
  correlating exit-0 test execution). Text from other sources — quoted,
  echoed, streamed by the wrong agent, or from an unattributed session —
  never flips state; it is journaled `suppressed`.
- The waiver and approval markers (`USER WAIVER:`, `PLAN APPROVED:`) are read
  only from the user's own prompt at admission — a marker inside an
  agent-composed dispatch prompt unlocks nothing, and a prompt-channel
  `PLAN APPROVED:` is honored exactly like a plan-reviewer verdict. The
  approval path via OpenCode's permission prompt is host-side UI, unreachable
  from session text. The dispatch-prompt waiver-forgery vector is closed; the
  residual trust stance (the journal is still the record of what was claimed)
  is unchanged.
- `scripts/check-markers.mjs` guards against accidental drift, not forgery.

Against hostile agents, use OpenCode's permission and sandboxing
mechanisms. Turnstile's value is the journal: it records what was claimed,
blocked, and waived.

## Attack surface: the journal

The plugin writes telemetry outside the repo at
`~/.local/share/opencode/metrics/` (or `$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/metrics`):

- `turnstile.jsonl`: dispatch descriptions, gate/verdict markers, bash
  command text (up to 500 chars, only when `trace` is enabled — otherwise
  journaled as `"<redacted>"`), read counts, errors
- `gate-events.log`: human-readable event lines

Both files default to world-readable permissions implied by the directory
(0755/0644). Bash commands and dispatch descriptions can contain secrets,
hostnames, and paths. Retention is bounded at ~30 MB per journal
(1 current + 5 rotated generations × 5 MB), ~60 MB worst case across the
two files. `gate-events.log` only exists while `trace: true` (the
default) and rotates on the same bounds, so `trace: false` roughly halves
the footprint.

Setting `trace: false` (or `TURNSTILE_TRACE=0`) suppresses the
human-readable trace file entirely and redacts bash command text
(`"<redacted>"`), dispatch descriptions (`""`), and waiver quotes
(`"<present>"`) from the JSONL journal. The JSONL journal itself always
writes; it is the audit trail.

If the journal contents are sensitive in your environment, protect the
metrics directory (e.g. user-only permissions) or point `metricsDir` at an
encrypted location.

The read side treats the journal as untrusted data, not a trust root: boot
replay shape-validates every line before applying it — session IDs failing
the ID-shape check are dropped and never become state keys, out-of-range
ensemble counts clamp, and plan identity fields that fail shape degrade to
unbound so the existing staleness validation applies. Each dropped line is
journaled as a replay-inert `suppressed` audit entry, so a hostile append is
observable. A single appended line can no longer mint a session bucket or
flip a restored gate. Protecting the metrics directory above remains the
actual boundary against a local writer.

## The published summary

`opencode-turnstile evidence` is the only path by which journal-derived data
is meant to leave the machine, and it is a whitelist projection, not an
excerpt: the document is assembled from permitted keys (derived counts,
canonical `GATE:`/`VERDICT:` marker lines, a one-way task handle, and the
sha256 of the most recent journaled line), so the fields above — session
paths and IDs, bash command text, dispatch descriptions — are absent by
construction rather than redacted after the fact. `evidence --validate`
re-asserts that in CI, rejecting any artifact carrying a session-ID-shaped or
path-shaped value.

What it cannot do is make the claim true. The summary reports what the journal
_claims_, in the same terms as the threat model above: a correlated claim, not
proof. It carries the journal head sha precisely so a reader can ask the
author for the raw journal and check the excerpt's tail.

9. Confirm the original failure is resolved.

You are the implementation agent.

You receive an implementation plan produced by another agent. Your job is to
implement that plan in the existing codebase. Do not redesign the system
unless the plan is demonstrably incompatible with the existing
implementation.

Note: turnstile's gates enforce once the pipeline is engaged (a plan
approval, a plan/dispatch prompt, or a planner dispatch); a parent that
started dormant may carry no prior gate state at your dispatch — the gates
fire normally from then on.

## Execution sequence

Work the plan chunk in this order, without deliberating about process:

1. Read the requirements specification and the implementation plan at the
   path the task provides — always use the path the task provides, never a
   default location (the plans directory is configurable). If either is
   missing (non-git directory, no plan produced, or not provided), report
   which is absent and stop. Read the source files the chunk names, their
   immediate interfaces, callers, and tests. Record the starting state:
   `git status` and `git diff` must be clean, or report the pre-existing
   changes and exclude them from your diff.
2. Implement, making the smallest reasonable change.
3. Run the narrowest relevant test once ≥2 files have changed. Repeat
   code → test until green.
4. Inspect the complete diff (`git diff` and `git diff --stat`), commit
   with a conventional message, and report.

Do not narrate deliberation. When the plan specifies an option, execute it.
When a choice is genuinely unmade, pick the plan-consistent option, record
one line under "Deviations", and continue.

## Constraints

- Make the smallest reasonable change; do not modify unrelated files.
- Reuse existing abstractions; follow the conventions visible in the files
  you read.
- Do not silently change requirements; do not add speculative features.
- Judge tests by actual command exit codes, never assumptions.

## Discrepancy protocol

If any of these occur, stop and report in three lines — Observed / Plan
reference / Blocker — then run the narrowest relevant test and continue
unless the discrepancy is unresolved:

- (a) more than 5 files must change;
- (b) the change touches a subsystem absent from the plan;
- (c) the plan contradicts the code;
- (d) 10 tool calls pass without running a test command — cite the plan
  step you are resuming in one line and resume.

If a task presented as small turns out to require substantial architectural
reasoning, that is a discrepancy under (c): report it instead of
improvising.

## Worktree / commit

Follow the worktree and commit rules in your task policy. Do not create,
add, remove, or switch worktrees or branches, merge, or open/close a PR
unless the user explicitly asks. If a worktree is in use, assert a
`WORKTREE:` header for logging.

## Completion

You are not finished merely because the code compiles. The implementation
is complete only when:

- The requested behavior exists.
- Acceptance criteria are satisfied.
- Relevant tests pass (verified by actual command exit codes, not
  assumptions).
- No obvious unrelated changes exist.
- The final diff has been inspected.

Report at the end:

- Files changed (with one-line reason each)
- Commands run and their exit codes
- Deviations from the plan (or "None")
- Acceptance criteria status (each: PASS/FAIL + evidence)

   assertion the change is about to break.

   each condition, early return, optional argument, and new case — and
   pair it with the test case that exercises both sides, in `# Tests`.

  implies it, it is an Open Question, not an implied requirement)

- Non-goals (what is explicitly out of scope)
- Acceptance criteria (objectively verifiable conditions for done)

- Base every requirement on the request text alone. Repository reads are
  NOT used to infer or justify requirements — anything that would need
  repository evidence to decide is a question for the planner, recorded in
  "Open Questions", not a requirement here.
- Do not invent requirements.
- If something is ambiguous, identify the ambiguity in "Open Questions"
  rather than silently choosing an interpretation.
- Every acceptance criterion must be objectively verifiable — a test, a
  command exit code, or an observable behavior. "Works correctly" is not
  an acceptance criterion.
- Every implied requirement must trace to something in the request. If you
  cannot name what implies it, move it to "Open Questions".
- The spec states what must hold, never how. Technology and design choices
  belong to the planner. If the user explicitly fixed a choice, record it
  under "Constraints" citing the user's words.
- Record explicit delegations. A user answer like "use your judgment" is a
  delegation: write it in "Explicit Requirements" or "Constraints" with its
  scope (what was delegated and over what), never absorb it silently.
- Keep the output compact. No prose padding.

# Objective

One paragraph: what will exist after this task is done.

# Explicit Requirements

Numbered list.

# Implied Requirements

Numbered list. Each item cites what in the request implies it (e.g. "implied
by the request's 'passed verbatim to the planner' phrase"). Write
"None identified" if empty.

# Constraints

Numbered list. Write "None identified" if empty.

# Non-Goals

Numbered list. Write "None identified" if empty.

# Acceptance Criteria

Numbered AC-1, AC-2, … AC-n. This numbering is authoritative: downstream
reviewers reference criteria as AC-<n>. Each criterion must be
independently checkable and must name the requirement(s) it verifies
(e.g. "AC-1 — verifies R1, R2"). No orphan criteria: every AC maps to at
least one requirement, and every explicit or implied requirement is covered
by at least one AC.

Numbered list of ambiguities the user should resolve. Mark each as
**blocking** (the planner cannot proceed without an answer) or
**non-blocking** (the planner may proceed with a recorded assumption).

"None" if the request is unambiguous.

# Turnstile — Architecture

Turnstile is an OpenCode v2 promise-plugin that mechanically enforces an agent
pipeline (**planner → plan-reviewer → executor → test-runner → reviewer**; an
optional, default-off requirements leg may precede the planner) by
interposing on the host's hook surface: every dispatch, read, shell call, and
user prompt is checked against per-parent gate state before it is allowed to
proceed. Enforcement is fail-open except for deliberate
`BLOCKED by turnstile:` errors.

Three ideas explain the whole plugin:

1. **A contract of markers.** Pipeline subagents emit machine-checkable first
   lines: the test-runner emits
   `GATE: PASS tests=<n> passed=<n> failed=<n>`; the reviewers emit
   `VERDICT: APPROVE|BLOCK crit=<n> high=<n> med=<n> low=<n>` (see
   `agents/test-runner.md`, `agents/reviewer.md`, `agents/plan-reviewer.md`).
   The planner emits no marker. Instead it produces numbered `AC-n` /
   `chunk-N` entries that the executor must cite and the plan gate scans for
   (`## Decomposition` in `.opencode/plans/`).
2. **Per-parent gate state.** Every session that admits a user prompt becomes a
   _parent_ (`ledger.markParent`). Gate flags, round counters, and the read
   budget all key off the parent via the `childToParent` edge map. A
   subagent's reads and dispatches draw down its parent's budget, never its
   own.
3. **Fail-open plumbing, fail-toward-strict enforcement.** Hook bodies catch
   their own errors and journal them; only deliberate `BlockError` decisions
   reach the host. Where evidence can go stale (plan edits), the plugin
   invalidates approvals rather than trusting them.

## Marker quick-reference

Pipeline subagents emit machine-checkable markers as the first line of their
output. The test-runner emits the gate marker; the reviewers emit the verdict
marker:

```text
GATE: PASS tests=12 passed=12 failed=0
VERDICT: APPROVE crit=3 high=1 med=0 low=0
```

A `GATE: FAIL tests=… passed=… failed=…` un-greens an earlier PASS
(latest-wins), and a `VERDICT: BLOCK crit=… high=… med=… low=…` sends the
plan back to the planner. The full semantics live in
[usage/worked-session.md](usage/worked-session.md) and
[architecture/gates.md](architecture/gates.md).

# Gate state machine

All state is keyed per parent session. `replayGrace` gives restart-restored
flags a one-prompt survival window; continuation carry (default on) re-arms
it when a continuing prompt has an unchanged worktree fingerprint and earned
credit (a green test gate or a reviewer approval). A retired task's credit
also rides the same window when the review phase was interrupted mid-flight:
a green test gate, at least one counted reviewer dispatch or waived reviewer
round, and no credited reviewer approval (`isInterruptedReview`,
`src/task-scope.ts`); both the live abort path and the restart-replay path
recover identically, and the journaled `continuation` row carries
`recovery: true` in that case. The recovery re-opens the retired task's
plan-bound scope, which then persists like any live plan-bound green task
(bounded by the ensemble cap and the landing gate, not by prompt count).

### Dormant-until-engaged

Enforcement is dormant by default (`alwaysEnforce: false`). A fresh session's
reactive gates (the dispatch guards for plan, decomposition, budget, and the
reviewer ensemble; the hands-on and bash-write ladders; the landing gate; the
commit lint; and the read horizon) sleep until the pipeline engages. The
user-configured denylists (`toolPolicy.bashDeny` / `toolPolicy.pathDeny`) and
all telemetry (dispatch, landing, hands-on, scratch rows) keep running while
dormant, so the audit trail stays complete. The `engaged` flag on the parent
bucket arms enforcement:

- **Arm**: a prompt carrying the `PLAN APPROVED:` marker (reason
  `plan-approved`), a prompt classified `plan-ref` or `dispatch` by the
  intent classifier (reasons `plan-reference` / `dispatch-request`), or an
  actual planner dispatch (reason `dispatch-request`). Every transition
  journals a `type:"engagement"` row.
- **Sleep**: task retire (`markTaskComplete`, reason `task-complete`), the
  `TURNSTILE OFF:` suspend clear (reason `abort`), and a scope-changing new
  prompt with no continuation credit (reason `continuation-drop`; on a
  carry, `mergeAfterReplay` preserves `engaged` like the other
  restart-sticky flags, and replay restores it last-wins from the journal).
- **Hint**: while dormant, a `work`/`issue`-intent prompt produces exactly
  the existing one-time advisory nudge; a dispatch/plan-ref prompt journals
  its `intent` row but never nudges (engagement replaced the reminder).
  The orchestrator policy head is also gated: a dormant session's context
  and deliveries stay clean of pipeline governance prose.

`alwaysEnforce: true` restores the legacy always-armed behavior in one
branch of the `enforcementArmed` predicate consulted at the four choke
points (`guardedTaskDispatch`, `handleBashDispatch`, `handleWriteEditDispatch`,
`handleReadBudget`); the guards themselves are unchanged.

# Hooks: where the plugin intercepts the host

Before any registration, `setup(h)` runs the host-compat guard
(`src/host-compat.ts`): the host version (`app.version`) is compared against
the shipped range (`HOST_COMPAT`, ≥ 2.0.22 and < 3.0.0). An **incompatible**
host is journaled (`type:"compat"`, `event:"incompatible"`), toasted with the
upgrade instruction, and turnstile degrades to a full no-op: no hook is
registered and the heartbeat carries `compat:"incompatible"`. An **unknown**
host (version unreadable or unparseable) enforces as usual and journals a
one-time `compat` warning (`event:"unknown-host"`); its heartbeat reads
`compat:"unknown"`. A **compatible** host proceeds byte-identically to the
pre-guard behavior with `compat:"compatible"` on the heartbeat. The guard is
fail-open: evaluation or toast failures are journaled, never thrown.

`setup(h)` then registers eight interception points, each tracked for disposal and
counted into the load heartbeat (`type:"setup"`). The hook bodies live in the
per-surface modules named below; `setup.ts` wires them and owns the lifecycle.

**`session.hook` ×4** (`hooks-session.ts`)

- **`prompt`** → `admitPrompt` (`prompt-admission.ts`): the single
  prompt-admission body, shared with the inbox stream and deduped on the
  host message id. Its concerns, in order:
  - _Admission and reset._ The body marks the session a live parent and
    performs `resetState`. When the worktree is unchanged, continuation
    carry rides along via `fingerprint.ts`. The reset releases the
    session's edge-registered children's metering counters; freeing at
    least one journals `type:"child-reset"`. It also clears evidence and
    latches.
  - _Waiver and approval capture._ The body captures `USER WAIVER:` /
    `PLAN APPROVED:` literals. A waiver capture also parses its scope, the
    configured agent names named in the waiver text (`parseWaiverScope` in
    `src/markers.ts`), into `userWaiverScope`.
  - _Suspend and resume._ `captureSuspend` scans for the configured
    `suspendMarker` / `resumeMarker` literals (defaults `TURNSTILE OFF:` /
    `TURNSTILE ON:`) by strict `indexOf`; the later-occurring marker wins,
    and the winning action is journaled `type:"suspended"`. An OFF suspends
    enforcement for the session (fresh-start state clear via `clearState`,
    no restart-sticky merge); an ON resumes it (also fresh: no credit
    earned while suspended rehydrates). When `allowSuspend:false`, both
    markers are refused: journaled `refused:true` (with the refused
    marker's `action`) plus a parked marker-style diagnostic; no state
    changes, and the refused entry folds replay-inert (a refusal can never
    resurrect a suspension after a restart). When an allowed OFF shares the
    prompt with `PLAN APPROVED:` or `USER WAIVER:`, the waiver/approval is
    captured first and then wiped by the fresh-start clear (the clear is
    authoritative), with a skip notice journaled.
  - _Near-miss diagnostics._ The body scans the text for marker-shaped
    near misses of the two literals (case, separator, or colon variants).
    This is diagnostic-only: the strict literal capture is untouched, the
    hits are journaled `type:"marker"` and parked for one-shot surfacing.
  - _Intent nudge._ Under `intentNudge` (default on), admission also
    classifies the prompt via `classifyIntent` (`src/intent.ts`). A
    detected implementation intent with no plan approval in the same
    admission journals `type:"intent"` (sessionID + signal kind) and arms
    a one-shot advisory nudge (one nudge per detected intent signal per
    session; a plan approval clears the latch). The nudge is delivered by
    prepending marker-syntax-free advisory prose to the first task
    delivery or the parent's own read delivery (`prependIntentNudge` /
    `prependIntentNudgeRead` in `hooks-core.ts`'s delivery helpers, text
    from `intentNudge` in `src/policy.ts`). Advisory only: nothing gates,
    and a throw in classification journals `type:"error"` and never
    propagates from the prompt path.
  - _Decision-ledger capture._ `captureLedgerBody`
    (`src/prompt-admission.ts`), placed after the dedupe check and after
    the approval/waiver capture sequence, journals one `prov:stated` entry
    per admitted parent prompt, verbatim after redaction, capped at 2000
    chars, no relevance filtering ("continue" included). Pipeline-child
    dispatch prompts are skipped, and the capture is gated on
    `decisionLedger.enabled` (default `true`, [configuration](configuration.md)). Because it lives inside
    the single deduped admission body, both transport paths (the prompt
    hook and the inbox stream) capture exactly once.
- **`generate`** → decoding clamps (`applyClamps`): reviewer/plan-reviewer
  temperature forced to 0; executor/test-runner/debugger clamped ≤ 0.2, plus
  one-per-boot draft telemetry (`observeRequestDraft`, a bounded
  `type:"generate-draft"` descriptor). Background generations (goal judge,
  warming) stay clean of policy prose.
- **`context`** → the primary-turn surface (pre-first-model-call; on v2.2.x
  hosts the main conversation turn fires `session.context`, not
  `session.generate`). Its concerns:
  - _Clamps and draft observation._ The body applies the same decoding
    clamps via the shared `applyClamps` helper (registering both hooks
    repairs the clamp gap: primary turns never rode `session.generate`)
    and observes the draft once per boot.
  - _Policy injection._ `injectContextPolicy` (`context-surface.ts`)
    injects the orchestrator policy head (`orchestratorPolicyFor`) and any
    pending intent nudge into the draft's `system` array in place; the
    host builds the model request from the same object, so the prose
    precedes the first model call.
  - _Parent guard._ Injection is parent-guarded: a config-known pipeline
    agent name on the draft, a registered child→parent edge
    (`ledger.childToParent`), or an unresolvable session id each skips
    with a journaled `reason` (`context-agent` / `context-child` /
    `context-no-id`).
  - _Shared latch._ The shared `policyInjected` latch (src/state.ts)
    dedupes against the `execute.after` prepend (whichever channel fires
    first wins), and the nudge is consumed one-shot from the same pending
    map.
  - _Fail-open degradation._ An unusable draft shape journals one
    `type:"error"` row per boot and degrades to the `execute.after`
    fallback channel; a head append failure keeps the nudge pending;
    nothing ever throws.
- **`compaction`** → appends a system block demanding verbatim preservation of
  open findings, AC status, and the last GATE/VERDICT markers, then the live
  gate-state snapshot (`formatGateSnapshot`) from the ledger, so the demand
  arrives with the concrete state beside it. The snapshot's `GATE:`/`VERDICT:` tokens are de-tokenized
  (leading token lowercased) so it can never re-parse as an authoritative
  marker. It reads, never mints, the parent bucket via `ledger.peek`,
  keyed off `draft.sessionID` and falling back to the last-admitted parent
  whenever parent resolution yields no bucket; both paths degrade to
  instruction-only (fail-open, no mint, no journal spam).

**`tool.hook("execute.before")`** (`hooks-tool.ts`): _all gating lives here_:

- `task`/`subagent`: dispatch budget (16 total), per-leg caps

  consulted only while `requirementsPhase` is on), plan-approval gate,

- `read`: parent-keyed read horizon (warn at 8 whole-file reads, once per task; block at 15).
- `bash`/`shell`: bash denylist → commit-message lint → hands-on bash

  executor's own work and never gates, keyed off the event's agent name with
  the child→parent edge + emitter fallback behind it (`resolveChildStatus`),
  fail-closed on an unresolved agent, after the telemetry row is journaled;
  while a plan is bound, a gate-tier write command is first classified
  against the plan's scope by the plan-impact advisory (containment
  matching on the command text), and an overlapping command is allowed with
  a journaled `plan-impact` row instead of the block, `planImpactStrict`

  → landing gate (with the empty-diff
  exemption, default on: ref-equality with upstream, force pushes always

- `write`/`edit`: a guard chain, evaluated in order:
  - _Denylist._ The path denylist decides first; its decision wins over
    everything below.
  - _Scratch exemption._ A target resolving under the platform temp dir is
    zero-governance scratch work, allowed with a
    `{type:"tool", scratch:true}` audit row carrying the target path,
    before any once-grant consume or ladder run.
  - _Child exemption._ The hands-on gate covers parent sessions and
    non-pipeline subagents; a registered pipeline child's write/edit is
    the executor's own work and never gates. The exemption keys off the
    event's agent name first (a configured pipeline name alone exempts),
    with the child→parent edge + emitter fallback behind it
    (`resolveChildStatus`), so an unresolved or non-pipeline agent fails
    closed. The denylist decision wins first and the journal reasons stay
    disjoint.
  - _Planner write-target guard._ Inside the child exemption, a planner
    child's write/edit is additionally confined to the configured
    `plansDir`. The agent name resolves by the same precedence (event name
    first, emitter fallback second; an unresolved name is not a planner —
    fail-open). Scratch targets and empty paths are allowed. A target
    outside the configured plans directory (resolved against the session's
    project dir, relative and absolute `plansDir` both honored) journals
    `{type:"blocked", reason:"planner-write-outside-plans-dir"}` and
    throws `BLOCKED by turnstile:` naming the configured directory and the
    corrective action; an internal error journals `type:"error"` and never
    blocks.
  - _Plan-impact advisory._ While a plan is bound and the session is
    engaged, the advisory runs after the once-grant consume: a target
    overlapping the plan's scope (equality matching on the path; the plan
    file itself is always structural) is allowed with a journaled
    `plan-impact` row and a one-shot advisory prepended to the next
    delivery instead of the block. `planImpactStrict: true` restores the
    block for structural overlap only. An equality target outside the
    project dir classifies `uninspectable` and falls through to the
    hands-on ladder with no journal row. With no plan bound the hands-on
    ladder is unchanged.
